**Wire verb `quant median-polish`**: Roll a FlashLFQ QuantifiedPeptides.tsv up to protein intensities per sample with FlashLFQ's median polish, under a new experimental design, without re-reading any spectra.

# Wraps

- [`FlashLfqResults.CalculateProteinResultsMedianPolish`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/23c2490e/mzLib/FlashLFQ/FlashLFQResults.cs) in `mzLib/FlashLFQ/FlashLFQResults.cs` at mzLib `23c2490e`
- [`FlashLfqResults.WriteResults`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/23c2490e/mzLib/FlashLFQ/FlashLFQResults.cs) in `mzLib/FlashLFQ/FlashLFQResults.cs` at mzLib `23c2490e`
- [`ProteinGroup`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/23c2490e/mzLib/FlashLFQ/ProteinGroup.cs) in `mzLib/FlashLFQ/ProteinGroup.cs` at mzLib `23c2490e`
- [`SpectraFileInfo`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/23c2490e/mzLib/MassSpectrometry/SpectraFileInfo.cs) in `mzLib/MassSpectrometry/SpectraFileInfo.cs` at mzLib `23c2490e`

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `peptides` (wire `--peptides`) | `path` | required | — | — | A FlashLFQ QuantifiedPeptides.tsv. Columns are found by header name: Sequence, Base Sequence and Protein Groups are required; Gene Names (or Gene Name) and Organism are optional; one Intensity\_&lt;run&gt; per run, each optionally with a Detection Type\_&lt;run&gt;. A blank intensity cell is 0 (not measured). |
| `design` (wire `--stdin`) | `string[]` | absent | — | `none, or exactly one line per Intensity_ run` | The experimental design, one run per line, tab-separated: run\_name\[TAB condition\[TAB biorep\[TAB techrep\[TAB fraction\]\]\]\], run\_name matching an Intensity\_&lt;run\_name&gt; column (a name, never opened as a file). Omitted fields: condition "", biorep = the line's 0-based index, techrep 0, fraction 0. With no lines at all, every Intensity\_ column is its own biological replicate with a blank condition, as FlashLFQ assumes with no design file. Median polish groups runs by condition and biological replicate, so this is how a caller says which runs are replicates of which sample. |
| `use_shared_peptides` (wire `--shared-peptides`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Let peptides shared between protein groups contribute (UseSharedPeptidesForProteinQuant). Off: a group with only shared peptides quantifies to 0. |
| `output_directory` (wire `--out`) | `path` | absent | — | — | Directory (created if absent) where FlashLFQ also writes QuantifiedProteins.tsv. Absent or blank writes nothing. |

# Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `peptides_file` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the peptide table. |
| `parameters` | `object` | — | never | {use\_shared\_peptides\_for\_protein\_quant}. |
| `samples` | `object[]` | — | never | One per (condition, biological replicate), ordered by condition (ordinal) then biorep, as the engine orders them; fields under result.tables.samples. Their labels are the keys of every protein's intensities. |
| `peptide_count` | `int` | peptides | never | Distinct sequences read from the table (rows with a Sequence). |
| `protein_count` | `int` | protein groups | never | Entries in proteins. |
| `proteins` | `object[]` | — | never | One per protein group, ordered by protein\_group (ordinal); fields under result.columns. |
| `output_directory` | `string` | — | yes: out was not given (or was blank): nothing was written | Absolute path of out. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `protein_group` | `string` | — | never | Protein group name; a ';'-joined Protein Groups cell is split into one group per name. |
| `gene_name` | `string` | — | never | From the table's gene column, paired to the group by position when the counts match, else the whole ';'-joined cell; "" when the table has no gene column. |
| `organism` | `string` | — | never | As gene\_name, from the Organism column. |
| `intensities` | `map<string,float>` | intensity (instrument units) | never | Sample label -&gt; protein intensity. A value is null when median polish could not resolve one (NaN: a degenerate peptide matrix); 0 means not measured in that sample. A sample of several runs (fractions, technical replicates) reports their sum, as FlashLFQ's own output does. |

Fields of each entry of `samples`:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | — | never | The run name when no design groups runs (every condition blank or Default, and one fraction); otherwise '&lt;condition&gt;\_&lt;biorep + 1&gt;', e.g. control\_1. |
| `condition` | `string` | — | never | The sample's condition; "" with no design. |
| `biological_replicate` | `int` | — | never | 0-based (the label adds 1). |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | peptides missing or blank, or not found; the file empty; a required column (Sequence, Base Sequence, Protein Groups) missing; no Intensity\_ columns; a sequence on two rows; an intensity cell that is not a number; a Detection Type\_ cell that is not a FlashLFQ DetectionType name |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | a design line with no run name, a run named twice, or a replicate/fraction that is not a non-negative integer; design runs with no Intensity\_ column; Intensity\_ runs the design does not mention (a design must name every run and only those) |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | FlashLFQ's reconstruction or median polish fails |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- Detection types: where the table has no Detection Type\_ column for a run (or the cell is blank), a positive intensity is treated as MSMS and 0 as NotDetected. That is this verb's only inference; a present but unrecognised value is an error, not a guess.
- Protein intensity null means unquantifiable, 0 means not measured; neither is a measured zero.
- Runs are names, not files: nothing but the peptide table is opened, and peak-level information (MBR peaks, retention times) is not available here. Use quant flashlfq for those.
- With out, QuantifiedProteins.tsv labels its columns by the same rule as samples\[\].label at this pin (mzLib\#1129 is in 23c2490e). Before \#1129 the file's rule was inverted for unfractionated data; the values always agreed.
